purpose: Authentic concept practice for lessons, revision, fast finishers and source-grounded relief learning.
boundary: Every saved record is formative practice only. It is not formal assessment, folio submission, teacher-observed evidence or a competence decision.

storage.autosave: Debounced browser-local save with visible local timestamp.
storage.reset: Reset one activity at a time after confirmation; never clear folio, quiz or assessment acknowledgement records.
storage.export: Plain-text or printable activity record with prompt context; creating an export does not submit it.

accessibility.interaction: All sorting, sequencing and matching mechanics must provide buttons or selects as an alternative to drag and drop.
accessibility.keyboard: Logical tab order, visible focus, labelled controls and a no-pointer completion path.
accessibility.touch: Controls remain usable at exactly 390 CSS pixels.
accessibility.feedback: Answer-neutral hints before response; specific success signals after self-check; no countdown or punitive colour-only state.
accessibility.print: Each activity has a low-tech version with the same thinking and durable evidence prompt.

activities.title: Career values trade-off grid
activities.placement: After the section explanation and before the higher-order response.
activities.practice: Use personal priorities and source evidence to compare career directions without treating a first choice as fixed.
activities.instructions: Choose two plausible directions, select four relevant criteria, add evidence for each and explain one trade-off.
activities.durable_evidence_prompt: Which criterion changed your ranking most, and what evidence made it important?
activities.feedback: A strong comparison names evidence, acknowledges a trade-off and keeps the decision provisional.
activities.printable_option: Two-column career comparison grid with four blank criteria rows and a decision rationale box.
activities.accessibility_alternative: Radio groups and text fields replace any draggable ranking.
activities.alt_text: Comparison grid for two career directions using evidence, priorities and trade-offs.

activities.title: Pathway evidence conference
activities.placement: After the change-and-sustainability explanation.
activities.practice: Test a pathway plan against change, barriers and alternative routes.
activities.instructions: Partner A presents a pathway and source evidence; Partner B asks what could change, what is controllable and what alternative remains. Swap, then revise.
activities.durable_evidence_prompt: Record the question that most improved your plan and the exact revision it caused.
activities.feedback: Useful revision identifies a dependency, adds a checkpoint or preserves a credible alternative.
activities.printable_option: Pathway conference sheet with evidence, challenge question and revision columns.
activities.accessibility_alternative: Complete the same challenge questions independently using the supplied scenario partner prompts.
activities.alt_text: Partner conference template for testing and revising a career pathway.

activities.title: Who connects to this role?
activities.placement: After workplace structures and relationships.
activities.practice: Investigate how one de-identified workplace role depends on information, decisions and support from others.
activities.instructions: Choose a fictional or public role, map four relationships and label what is exchanged, decided or clarified.
activities.durable_evidence_prompt: Where could a broken connection affect the work, and who should clarify responsibility?
activities.feedback: A useful map names the relationship purpose, not just job titles.
activities.printable_option: Blank role map with four relationship spokes and a breakdown analysis box.
activities.accessibility_alternative: Structured relationship table instead of a visual map.
activities.alt_text: Workplace role map linking people, information, responsibilities and support.

activities.title: Pause, check, act
activities.placement: After rights, responsibilities and safe participation; before any teacher-controlled practical direction.
activities.practice: Separate an observation, an uncertainty and a safe source of help in a workplace scenario.
activities.instructions: For each fictional situation, sort what is known, what must be checked and the safest next communication step. Do not invent a local procedure.
activities.durable_evidence_prompt: Choose one scenario and justify why checking with the nominated authority is safer than assuming.
activities.feedback: Strong responses identify uncertainty and use current teacher or workplace direction rather than guessing.
activities.printable_option: Three-column Known / Need to check / Safe next step scenario sheet.
activities.accessibility_alternative: Select menus and text fields provide the same sorting task without dragging.
activities.alt_text: Workplace scenarios sorted into known information, checks needed and safe next communication.

activities.title: Criteria-to-evidence match
activities.placement: After reading opportunities and selection criteria.
activities.practice: Distinguish required, desirable and contextual information, then match honest evidence to each criterion.
activities.instructions: Use a teacher-provided or redacted current opportunity. Annotate its requirements and mark each as evidence available, evidence weak or gap.
activities.durable_evidence_prompt: Which criterion needs a stronger example, and what realistic action could create evidence?
activities.feedback: A credible match uses a specific example and openly records unsupported gaps.
activities.printable_option: Opportunity annotation key and criteria-evidence-gap table.
activities.accessibility_alternative: Plain-text opportunity with labelled checkboxes and evidence fields.
activities.alt_text: Selection criteria table matching honest evidence and identifying gaps.

activities.title: Interview evidence carousel
activities.placement: After interview preparation and before the reflective application.
activities.practice: Build concise, evidence-based answers and listen for relevance.
activities.instructions: Use three supplied questions. One student answers for 60-90 seconds; the other records the claim, evidence and relevance, then roles swap.
activities.durable_evidence_prompt: Rewrite one answer so the evidence is clearer and the final sentence directly answers the question.
activities.feedback: A strong answer is relevant, truthful, concise and supported by a specific example.
activities.printable_option: Three-question rehearsal sheet with claim, evidence, relevance and revision boxes.
activities.accessibility_alternative: A written interview exchange may replace spoken rehearsal without changing the evidence task.
activities.alt_text: Interview rehearsal record linking each response to a claim, evidence and relevance check.

activities.title: Choose the channel
activities.placement: After purpose, audience and communication channels.
activities.practice: Choose a channel by purpose, audience, urgency, privacy and need for a record.
activities.instructions: For five fictional workplace messages, choose a channel and justify it using two decision factors.
activities.durable_evidence_prompt: Identify one scenario where your first choice changed after considering privacy or the need for a record.
activities.feedback: A defensible choice links the channel to the situation; there may be more than one suitable answer.
activities.printable_option: Scenario table with channel, two reasons and an alternative channel.
activities.accessibility_alternative: Radio buttons and justification fields; no drag interaction.
activities.alt_text: Workplace communication scenarios compared by purpose, audience, urgency, privacy and record needs.

activities.title: Repair the conversation
activities.placement: After feedback, conflict and communication repair.
activities.practice: Use listening, neutral language, clarification and a next step to repair misunderstanding.
activities.instructions: Read a fictional misunderstanding, perform the first response, pause for feedback, then replay it using neutral observation, clarification and an agreed next step.
activities.durable_evidence_prompt: Record the exact wording change that reduced blame and improved clarity.
activities.feedback: Effective repair separates the issue from the person and confirms what happens next.
activities.printable_option: Before / revised / why it is clearer conversation script.
activities.accessibility_alternative: Complete both dialogue versions in writing or with augmentative communication.
activities.alt_text: Two-pass conversation script showing a neutral communication repair.

activities.title: Team charter that can be used
activities.placement: After team roles, trust and shared goals.
activities.practice: Translate trust and shared goals into observable team behaviours.
activities.instructions: Write one shared goal, four observable behaviours, a check-in method and a fair way to raise a concern.
activities.durable_evidence_prompt: Which charter behaviour would be easiest to observe, and how would the team know it is happening?
activities.feedback: A usable charter describes actions the team can see and review, not vague personality labels.
activities.printable_option: One-page team charter with goal, behaviours, check-in and concern pathway.
activities.accessibility_alternative: Contributions may be spoken, typed or selected from neutral behaviour starters before group agreement.
activities.alt_text: Team charter connecting a shared goal to observable behaviours and review.

activities.title: Five-minute problem-solving stand-up
activities.placement: After initiative, problem-solving and decision-making.
activities.practice: Use a short structured cycle to define a problem, generate options and select a reviewable action.
activities.instructions: Use a low-risk fictional work problem. Define it in one sentence, generate three options, select one using evidence and nominate a review point.
activities.durable_evidence_prompt: What evidence made the selected option more defensible than the others?
activities.feedback: A sound decision states the problem, compares options and leaves a review point.
activities.printable_option: Problem / options / evidence / action / review stand-up card.
activities.accessibility_alternative: No enforced timer; the same turn-taking prompts can be completed asynchronously.
activities.alt_text: Structured team problem-solving record comparing options and setting a review point.

activities.title: Commitments map and boundary decision
activities.placement: After time, priorities and realistic boundaries.
activities.practice: Distinguish fixed, flexible and negotiable commitments in a fictional week.
activities.instructions: Use the supplied fictional week, classify commitments, protect recovery time and write one respectful boundary message.
activities.durable_evidence_prompt: Which commitment did you move or negotiate, and what priority did that protect?
activities.feedback: A sustainable plan recognises limits, communicates early and keeps essential commitments visible.
activities.printable_option: Weekly map with fixed, flexible, negotiate and recovery labels.
activities.accessibility_alternative: List view with category selects instead of a calendar drag interface.
activities.alt_text: Fictional weekly commitments sorted by flexibility with a boundary message.

activities.title: Plan B after change
activities.placement: After adapting plans across life stages.
activities.practice: Adapt a plan when time, location, income or caring commitments change.
activities.instructions: Draw one fictional change card, identify what stays, what changes, who must be contacted and the next review date.
activities.durable_evidence_prompt: Explain one choice that keeps the person's core goal while changing the route.
activities.feedback: Adaptation is not failure when the revised route protects purpose and responds to evidence.
activities.printable_option: Original plan / change / keep / revise / contact / review table.
activities.accessibility_alternative: Text-based change cards can be chosen from a labelled list.
activities.alt_text: Scenario table adapting a plan while preserving its core purpose.

activities.title: Read the pay record
activities.placement: After pay, tax, superannuation and records.
activities.practice: Locate and explain the purpose of common fields in a teacher-provided, fictional or current official sample pay record.
activities.instructions: Label the fields, trace gross-to-net relationships shown in the sample and list any value or rate that must be checked against a current official source.
activities.durable_evidence_prompt: Which two fields would you check first if the record did not match your expectation, and why?
activities.feedback: Strong annotation explains field purpose and flags current rates rather than memorising unsupported figures.
activities.printable_option: De-identified sample annotation sheet; no real payslip required.
activities.accessibility_alternative: Linear field list with descriptions replaces image hotspot labelling.
activities.alt_text: De-identified pay-record fields annotated by purpose and current-source check.

activities.title: Budget shock and buffer
activities.placement: After budgeting, banking, credit and saving.
activities.practice: Make a reasoned trade-off when a fictional budget changes.
activities.instructions: Use the supplied fictional budget, reveal one change, protect essentials, adjust two categories and explain the buffer or support strategy.
activities.durable_evidence_prompt: What did you protect first, what did you change and what consequence remains?
activities.feedback: A defensible budget names priorities and consequences; it does not pretend every pressure can be removed.
activities.printable_option: Fictional before-and-after budget with trade-off rationale.
activities.accessibility_alternative: Editable numeric fields and a calculation summary; no timed mental arithmetic.
activities.alt_text: Fictional budget revised after a change, showing priorities, trade-offs and a buffer.

activities.title: Workplace issue evidence matrix
activities.placement: After analysing impacts, evidence and perspectives.
activities.practice: Compare evidence quality and perspectives without turning a complex issue into a personal dispute.
activities.instructions: Use two teacher-provided or current public sources. Record claim, evidence, perspective, limitation and one question for each.
activities.durable_evidence_prompt: What conclusion is supported by both sources, and what remains uncertain?
activities.feedback: Careful analysis separates source evidence from inference and acknowledges limits.
activities.printable_option: Two-source evidence and perspective matrix.
activities.accessibility_alternative: Sources and prompts available as accessible text; group contribution may be written.
activities.alt_text: Matrix comparing claims, evidence, perspectives, limits and unanswered questions.

activities.title: Verify before responding
activities.placement: After response through policy, support and action.
activities.practice: Choose a proportionate response pathway and identify where current authoritative advice is required.
activities.instructions: For a fictional issue, sequence clarify, record, check current authority, seek support and review. Do not supply legal conclusions or local policy details.
activities.durable_evidence_prompt: Which step prevents the biggest unsupported assumption, and what source or person must be checked?
activities.feedback: A safe pathway distinguishes immediate support, fact checking and formal action.
activities.printable_option: Blank response pathway with a current-authority check box.
activities.accessibility_alternative: Numbered selects replace drag sequencing.
activities.alt_text: Source-safe workplace issue response pathway with verification and support steps.

activities.title: Need and strengths interview
activities.placement: After moving from strengths and needs to a viable idea.
activities.practice: Listen for a need, distinguish it from a solution and test fit with available strengths.
activities.instructions: Use a fictional prompt or consented classroom problem. Ask five neutral questions, summarise the need and list evidence that supports or challenges the idea.
activities.durable_evidence_prompt: What did you hear that changed your original idea, and why?
activities.feedback: A useful summary reflects the need accurately and does not force the first solution.
activities.printable_option: Five-question interview sheet with need, evidence and changed idea boxes.
activities.accessibility_alternative: Written scenario responses may replace live interviewing.
activities.alt_text: Structured interview record separating a need from a proposed solution.

activities.title: Micro-enterprise risk test
activities.placement: After business models, obligations and risk.
activities.practice: Identify assumptions, classify risk and choose a low-cost, ethical test before committing resources.
activities.instructions: For one fictional idea, list value, resource, obligation and demand assumptions. Rank by consequence and uncertainty, then design one small test.
activities.durable_evidence_prompt: Which assumption should be tested first, and what result would trigger continue, change or stop?
activities.feedback: A strong test is small, ethical, measurable and linked to a decision.
activities.printable_option: Assumption / risk / evidence / test / decision board.
activities.accessibility_alternative: Select-based ranking and text list replace draggable cards.
activities.alt_text: Micro-enterprise assumption and risk board linked to a small decision test.

activities.title: Project brief sprint
activities.placement: After defining the problem and project purpose.
activities.practice: Turn a broad problem into a shared purpose and observable success criteria.
activities.instructions: Use a teacher-approved project context. Draft who, need, purpose and boundaries, then agree on three observable success criteria.
activities.durable_evidence_prompt: Which criterion best proves the project purpose, and how will the team observe it?
activities.feedback: A useful brief defines the need and boundaries; criteria describe observable success rather than effort alone.
activities.printable_option: One-page project brief and success-criteria canvas.
activities.accessibility_alternative: Structured sentence fields and anonymous idea collection support equitable group contribution.
activities.alt_text: Team project brief linking a problem, user, purpose, boundaries and success criteria.

activities.title: Sprint review evidence pitch
activities.placement: During delivery and again before final evaluation.
activities.practice: Use evidence to communicate progress, a problem, a decision and the next action.
activities.instructions: Present one criterion, one evidence item, one problem and one next action. Listeners ask one evidence question and one feasibility question.
activities.durable_evidence_prompt: Record the question that caused the clearest change to the project plan.
activities.feedback: A strong pitch connects evidence to a criterion and turns feedback into a specific action.
activities.printable_option: Criterion / evidence / problem / decision / next action pitch card.
activities.accessibility_alternative: A written or pre-recorded text-supported pitch may replace live presentation; no student recording is stored by the site.
activities.alt_text: Project review pitch linking evidence, a problem, a decision and a next action.

activities.title: First-day preparation rehearsal
activities.placement: After preparation for workplace experience and only within approved local arrangements.
activities.practice: Ask for clarification, repeat back instructions and prepare a source-safe first-day plan.
activities.instructions: Use a generic scenario. Rehearse introduction, instruction check, clarification question and what to do when unsure. Add placement-specific directions only when the teacher confirms them.
activities.durable_evidence_prompt: Write the clarification question and repeat-back sentence that would reduce misunderstanding.
activities.feedback: Prepared participation includes respectful clarification and following authorised site directions; the activity does not prove competence.
activities.printable_option: First-day communication rehearsal card with local details left blank for current teacher direction.
activities.accessibility_alternative: Written dialogue or communication aid may replace spoken role-play.
activities.alt_text: Generic first-day workplace rehearsal focused on clarification and authorised directions.

activities.title: Observe, interpret, transfer
activities.placement: After an authorised observation, simulation or workplace experience.
activities.practice: Separate observation from interpretation and transfer one learning point to a next context.
activities.instructions: Record what you observed without names, interpret what it may mean, identify a question, then plan where to apply or test the learning next.
activities.durable_evidence_prompt: Which observation produced the most useful learning, and how will you test it elsewhere?
activities.feedback: A credible reflection distinguishes what happened, what you infer and what still needs checking.
activities.printable_option: Observation / interpretation / question / transfer ladder.
activities.accessibility_alternative: Text, speech-to-text or teacher-approved symbol-supported response; no photo is required.
activities.alt_text: De-identified reflection ladder moving from observation to interpretation, question and transfer.
